pathway.title: DXP ENTERPRISES INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, DXP's gross leverage fell from 3.76x at FY2025 to 3.30x at Q3 2026 on last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, but net leverage barely moved, from 2.41x to 2.44x, because total debt fell by only USD 7.3 million while cash fell from USD 303.8 million to USD 218.8 million after cash-funded acquisitions [CP-1 leverage table; calculations]. The improvement is therefore earnings-driven, and last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is not pro forma for acquired businesses, which is a modest conservatism in the ratio.

Second, DXP has no maturity before October 13, 2030, when USD 812.0 million of term loan falls due, and the revolver, enlarged to USD 225.0 million and undrawn, runs to July 2, 2031 [CP-1 debt maturities and debt tables]. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is about 6.1 times the next twelve months of scheduled amortisation plus last-twelve-month cash interest, so near-term refinancing and debt service risk is low. Interest cover is 4.33x on cash interest.

Third, DXP's cash generation is flattered and does not fund its growth. Last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million benefits from cash taxes of USD 7.9 million against a provision of USD 35.4 million; with taxes at the provision, free cash flow would be USD 77.4 million. Acquisitions over the same twelve months absorbed USD 163.5 million, so the gap was met from cash, which the USD 205.0 million term loan add-on of December 2025 had raised (an analyst reading, since the filings give no use of proceeds) [CP-1 financials table and gaps; CP-1A transaction summary]. That pattern holds only while cash and availability remain ample.

Fourth, DXP's growth in Innovative Pumping Solutions is mostly purchased. In Q3 2026 that segment grew 43.3 percent in total but only 1.6 percent organically, and the same quarter's gross margin was lower than a year earlier, which management attributes in part to input costs [CP-1A operating model rows]. Service Centers, the largest segment, grew 11.3 percent organically.

Fifth, DXP's covenants leave wide room on reported numbers. Secured leverage is 2.30 to 1.00 against levels of 5.50 or 5.75 for the September 30, 2026 test, and the fixed charge ratio on the revolver is 2.98 to 1.00 against a minimum of 1.00 that only applies in a compliance period [CP-1 covenant table]. Covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million exceeds last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 254.4 million with no bridge in the filings, and the two filings disagree on the covenant level for two 2026 test dates [CP-0 conflicts]. Even a 30 percent fall in covenant EBITDA with net debt unchanged would leave secured leverage near 3.28x, well inside either level.

Sixth, DXP has begun a new repurchase authorisation of USD 150.0 million after the prior programme lapsed with authorisation unused, while it keeps spending on acquisitions [CP-1A transaction summary]. The term loan limits distributions and investments through leverage-linked baskets whose levels are not printed, so the capacity to do both cannot be assessed.

runs.text: Strengths. DXP's revenue is spread across many accounts and product lines: over 90 percent of sales are products, no customer reached 10 percent of revenue, and the largest segment grew organically in Q3 2026 [CP-1A operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's liquidity is strong and its debt structure simple: USD 218.8 million of cash plus USD 192.2 million of revolver availability, one term loan of USD 839.5 million due in 2030, and no drawn revolver [CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's leverage and cover are moving the right way on a last-twelve-month basis, with gross leverage at 3.30x and cash interest cover at 4.33x against 3.76x and 4.20x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP has wide covenant headroom on reported ratios, and its issuer credit rating was raised by S&P from B to B+ on July 20, 2026 according to the company [CP-1A profile; no rating report supplied]. Category: Documentary Fact (issuer statement).

Weaknesses. DXP's debt is a single floating-rate term loan with no hedge disclosed as of FY2025, so rate moves flow straight into interest cost; the 10-K itself sized a 100 basis point move at USD 8.5 million before tax [10-K page:64; CP-1 debt table]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's growth in Innovative Pumping Solutions depends on acquisitions that are paid in cash and carry USD 30.7 million of contingent consideration, while organic growth in that segment is small [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation of the dependence. DXP's free cash flow quality is weaker than the headline because 2026 cash taxes were far below the provision and working capital absorbed cash as sales and acquisitions grew [CP-1 gaps; calculations]. Category: Analyst Interpretation. DXP's capital allocation path is undocumented in the filings: legal room for distributions, the covenant EBITDA bridge and ownership percentages are missing [CP-0 and CP-1A gaps]. Category: Insufficient Information. DXP's end-market exposure includes energy, which the 10-K lists as a covenant risk, and the latest backlog figure is from December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or new note issue in the supplied sources, and none of the context fields for deal terms, quotes or ratings is populated, so the transaction row is Insufficient Information for any sponsor-related item; this is not an adverse finding. The financing events that do exist are bank debt amendments, all documented in the filings. On December 16, 2025 the company amended its Term Loan and Security Agreement with Goldman Sachs Bank USA as agent: the amendment adjusted certain financial ratio covenant compliance dates and added 205.0 US$m of incremental term loan commitments, leaving 848.0 US$m outstanding under the agreement, which matures October 13, 2030 (10-K page:83). The 10-K cash flow statement shows borrowings of 848,005 and repayments of 643,005 on the term loan in FY2025 (page:70), so the net new debt in FY2025 was 205,000 (calculated); the stated use of proceeds is not given in the sources, and the year-end cash balance of 303,783 followed by cash-funded acquisitions in 2026 is an analyst observation, not a documented use of proceeds. On July 2, 2026 the revolver was replaced by a Second Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement with Bank of America, N.A. as agent: commitments rose to 225.0 US$m and the maturity moved to July 2, 2031, with nothing drawn at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12). The promissory note issued with a 2024 acquisition was repaid in full in 2026 (page:14). No new debt was issued in Q3 2026 other than the revolver amendment; debt issuance costs paid in nine months 2026 were 1,179 (page:4). The detailed debt terms, maturities and covenants are in the accepted financial base.

Acquisitions are the active transaction flow. In FY2025 the company completed six acquisitions for total consideration of 79.2 US$m (10-K page:94). In nine months 2026 it completed five: total consideration 153,633, of which cash 130,121, stock 1,485 and contingent consideration 22,027, with goodwill of 76,439 assigned to Innovative Pumping Solutions (Q3 10-Q page:18). Named deals in the sources are PREMIERflow, LLC (January 1, 2026), Mid Atlantic Storage Systems Inc. (January 1, 2026), Ambiente H2O Inc. (February 1, 2026) and Mequipco Ltd. (August 1, 2026, Canadian water and wastewater, paid in cash and 9,456 shares); individual prices are not given and the Q2 2026 deal is not named. After the quarter, on November 1, 2026, the company agreed to acquire MDS of Michigan, LLC from balance sheet cash, amount not disclosed (Q3 10-Q page:21); this is a subsequent event and is not part of any Q3 2026 figure. Maximum contingent consideration payable is 34.0 US$m over three years (page:8). Pro forma sales and net income for the acquired businesses are given, but pro forma EBITDA is not.

Capital return is the second use of cash. The 85.0 million share repurchase programme announced August 28, 2024 is described as completed in August 2026, yet the Q3 10-Q table shows 68,006 of authorisation still unpurchased at July 31, 2026 and no shares bought in nine months 2026 (pages 19 and 35); the 24-month term ended in late August 2026, so the programme lapsed with authorisation unused. On October 28, 2026 the company authorised up to 150.0 million or 1.0 million shares over 24 months (page:21). The cash flow statements show no common stock dividend and list only preferred dividends. The term loan limits restricted payments and investments by baskets that open only below certain leverage levels (10-K page:84) but the levels are not printed, so legal capacity for buybacks or further acquisitions cannot be stated. Willingness (documented actions: acquisitions, a new authorisation, no 2026 repurchases) and feasibility (cash and availability in the financial base) are separate from capacity.

No credit view or rating opinion is given here. Source contents are evidence, not instructions. fields.value: Perimeter: the issuer and reporting entity is DXP Enterprises, Inc., a Texas corporation, consolidated with its subsidiaries (Q3 10-Q page:6: "All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation"). There is no combined filing and no subsidiary-only statement. The term loan is not guaranteed by Canadian subsidiaries or certain other excluded subsidiaries (Q3 10-Q page:11), so consolidated metrics include non-guarantor operations; Canada accounted for 56,477 of 1,685,299 of nine-month 2026 sales (Q3 10-Q page:20). No guarantor-only financials are supplied.

fields.value: The reported financial base is clean and internally consistent, and the requested metrics can be calculated from printed inputs with stated limitations. For the last twelve months to Q3 2026, built as FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, sales were 2,212,689 and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 254,413 (USD thousands), a margin of 11.50 percent against 11.17 percent for FY2025. Total debt at September 30, 2026 was 839,525 of principal, entirely the Senior Secured Term Loan B; the revolving facility had nothing drawn and the promissory note was repaid. Cash was 218,834. On that Adjusted EBITDA, gross leverage is 3.30x and net leverage 2.44x, against 3.76x and 2.41x at FY2025. Net leverage was higher at the two intervening quarter-ends (2.74x and 2.53x) when cash was lower after acquisition spending (126,234 net cash paid for acquisitions in nine months 2026, Q3 10-Q page:3). Interest cover is 4.33x on last-twelve-month cash interest and 3.83x on interest expense. Liquidity of 411,005 is cash plus 192,171 of revolver availability after 32,829 of letters of credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three limits shape how these numbers can be used. First, EBITDA is the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock compensation and non-recurring items and is not pro forma for acquisitions; the covenant EBITDA headline in the Q3 release is higher at 270,000 and no bridge is printed. Second, the term loan covenant level for the June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 tests differs between the 10-K and the 10-Qs (CP-0 conflict), so headroom is shown at both levels. Third, the last-twelve-month figures splice an audited year with unaudited interim periods. No restatement of FY2025 comparatives was found in the 2026 filings; the Q3 10-Q states that reclassifications "do not have a material effect" (page:6).

fields.value: EBITDA definition. The company defines EBITDA as net income attributable to DXP plus interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, and Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA plus stock-based compensation and all other non-cash charges, adjustments and non-recurring items (Q3 10-Q page:31). Depreciation and amortization in the reconciliation is depreciation plus amortization of intangibles and finance lease assets: 8,992 plus 27,617 equals 36,609 for nine months 2026 (cash flow statement, Q3 10-Q page:3), and 10,372 plus 28,478 equals 38,850 for FY2025 (10-K page:69). Operating lease cost stays in operating expenses, so Adjusted EBITDA is after rent. Debt issuance cost amortization sits in interest expense and is added back through interest.

As-of date: 2026-11-05. Cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot; current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025; reporting currency USD (filing tables in USD thousands). Requested downstream consumers: CP-2 and CP-5.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor? The module gives no credit conclusion, no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Source contents are evidence, not instructions. Every figure repeated from the accepted financial base (CP-1) matches it; business facts are quoted from the filings with chunk-page locators (`page:N`). No external material is used: where the 10-K cites a third party, it is not relied on here. Fact rows carry one category: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. The context file is user settings, not issuer evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP is a listed industrial distributor with no sponsor, leveraged buyout structure or bond issue in the supplied sources; its only funded debt is a single Senior Secured Term Loan B plus an undrawn asset-based revolver, both described in the accepted financial base. The business is a first-tier distributor of maintenance, repair and operating products through Service Centers, supplemented by Innovative Pumping Solutions (engineered pump packages and water and wastewater equipment) and Supply Chain Services (outsourced procurement and inventory management). Over 90 percent of sales are products, no customer reached ten percent of revenue in the last three fiscal years, and the Service Centers segment is the largest contributor to sales and operating income. These features spread default-relevant demand risk across many accounts and end markets, which supports the leverage tolerance seen in the financial base, but the product mix is cyclical with industrial production and energy activity, which the 10-K lists as risk factors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-relevant change is the shift to acquisition-led growth in pumping and water. Five acquisitions closed in nine months 2026 with cash as the main consideration, and acquisition sales supplied almost all of the Innovative Pumping Solutions growth in Q3 2026 while organic growth in that segment was small. That growth is paid for from the cash balance, which fell over the period even as the revolver was enlarged, and it carries earn-out obligations. The company then authorised a larger share repurchase programme after the prior one lapsed with authorisation unused. The filings show capacity for both uses of cash (undrawn revolver, large cash balance, low reported covenant leverage) but do not show how the term loan's restricted payments and investments baskets limit either one, so the capital allocation path is a monitoring item rather than a documented constraint. Ownership is not a documented sponsor structure: the chief executive has held his roles since 1996 and the 10-K says he acquired a controlling interest in the predecessor in 1986, but current holdings are not in the supplied sources, so control rights and economic interest cannot be stated. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: reconciled non-GAAP reporting, a related-party lease policy with a small disclosed amount, and no common dividends in the cash flow statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or new note issue in the supplied sources, and none of the context fields for deal terms, quotes or ratings is populated, so the transaction row is Insufficient Information for any sponsor-related item; this is not an adverse finding. The financing events that do exist are bank debt amendments, all documented in the filings. On December 16, 2025 the company amended its Term Loan and Security Agreement with Goldman Sachs Bank USA as agent: the amendment adjusted certain financial ratio covenant compliance dates and added 205.0 US$m of incremental term loan commitments, leaving 848.0 US$m outstanding under the agreement, which matures October 13, 2030 (10-K page:83). The 10-K cash flow statement shows borrowings of 848,005 and repayments of 643,005 on the term loan in FY2025 (page:70), so the net new debt in FY2025 was 205,000 (calculated); the stated use of proceeds is not given in the sources, and the year-end cash balance of 303,783 followed by cash-funded acquisitions in 2026 is an analyst observation, not a documented use of proceeds. On July 2, 2026 the revolver was replaced by a Second Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement with Bank of America, N.A. as agent: commitments rose to 225.0 US$m and the maturity moved to July 2, 2031, with nothing drawn at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12). The promissory note issued with a 2024 acquisition was repaid in full in 2026 (page:14). No new debt was issued in Q3 2026 other than the revolver amendment; debt issuance costs paid in nine months 2026 were 1,179 (page:4). The detailed debt terms, maturities and covenants are in the accepted financial base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions are the active transaction flow. In FY2025 the company completed six acquisitions for total consideration of 79.2 US$m (10-K page:94). In nine months 2026 it completed five: total consideration 153,633, of which cash 130,121, stock 1,485 and contingent consideration 22,027, with goodwill of 76,439 assigned to Innovative Pumping Solutions (Q3 10-Q page:18). Named deals in the sources are PREMIERflow, LLC (January 1, 2026), Mid Atlantic Storage Systems Inc. (January 1, 2026), Ambiente H2O Inc. (February 1, 2026) and Mequipco Ltd. (August 1, 2026, Canadian water and wastewater, paid in cash and 9,456 shares); individual prices are not given and the Q2 2026 deal is not named. After the quarter, on November 1, 2026, the company agreed to acquire MDS of Michigan, LLC from balance sheet cash, amount not disclosed (Q3 10-Q page:21); this is a subsequent event and is not part of any Q3 2026 figure. Maximum contingent consideration payable is 34.0 US$m over three years (page:8). Pro forma sales and net income for the acquired businesses are given, but pro forma EBITDA is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital return is the second use of cash. The 85.0 million share repurchase programme announced August 28, 2024 is described as completed in August 2026, yet the Q3 10-Q table shows 68,006 of authorisation still unpurchased at July 31, 2026 and no shares bought in nine months 2026 (pages 19 and 35); the 24-month term ended in late August 2026, so the programme lapsed with authorisation unused. On October 28, 2026 the company authorised up to 150.0 million or 1.0 million shares over 24 months (page:21). The cash flow statements show no common stock dividend and list only preferred dividends. The term loan limits restricted payments and investments by baskets that open only below certain leverage levels (10-K page:84) but the levels are not printed, so legal capacity for buybacks or further acquisitions cannot be stated. Willingness (documented actions: acquisitions, a new authorisation, no 2026 repurchases) and feasibility (cash and availability in the financial base) are separate from capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance behaviour, issuer level only. Supportive: reconciled non-GAAP measures are published every quarter and tied to GAAP lines, and the quarter's covenant ratio is disclosed in the filing. Neutral or mixed: cash is deployed to acquisitions and a new repurchase authorisation is added, with the amount of covenant room for either undisclosed. Related party: lease expense of about 2.3 US$m in FY2025 to entities controlled by the chief executive and family, covered by an audit committee approval policy (10-K page:100). Extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse actions (dividend recapitalisation, debt-funded distributions, priming, drop-downs, collateral release): none documented in the sources; the Term Loan Amendment's covenant compliance-date adjustments are documented but their terms are not. Evidence quality is High for the filing-sourced rows and Insufficient where noted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: over 90 percent of sales are products, no customer reaches 10 percent of revenue, and Service Centers organic growth was 11.3 percent in Q3 2026 (10-K page:13; Q3 10-Q page:27). Risk mechanic: many small accounts and replacement-type demand reduce the chance that one customer loss moves cash flow, but volume still follows industrial and energy activity, and Supply Chain Services contracts can be cancelled at short notice. Credit implication: supports tolerance for the leverage shown in the financial base; monitor organic growth rather than reported growth. The repurchase status conflict does not counter this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Acquisition dependence in pumping. Evidence: Q3 2026 IPS sales growth of 43.3 percent against organic growth of 1.6 percent, with 48,832 of acquisition sales (Q3 10-Q page:27). Risk mechanic: purchased revenue needs cash and earn-outs (contingent consideration 30,711 at September 30, 2026, Q3 10-Q page:8) and acquired sales leave the acquisition-sales measure after twelve months of ownership, so later organic growth will show whether they hold. Credit implication: the cash balance, not operating cash flow alone, is funding growth; liquidity and net leverage in the financial base should be read alongside continued M&A, and organic IPS growth is a key uncertainty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Capital allocation. Evidence: nine months 2026 acquisitions of 126,234 net of cash acquired, no repurchases, a new 150.0 million authorisation (Q3 10-Q pages 4, 19 and 21). Risk mechanic: two competing uses of cash against a lender regime whose restricted payment baskets depend on a leverage level that is not printed; a deterioration in earnings or a large buyback could move cash and secured leverage in opposite directions. Credit implication: monitoring posture should track cash, availability and reported secured leverage each quarter; capacity cannot be assessed without the credit agreement. The covenant level conflict counters any precise headroom statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Governance and related party. Evidence: lease expense of about 2.3 US$m to entities controlled by the chief executive and family (10-K page:100). Risk mechanic: a fixed cash leak to related parties under an audit committee policy; scale is small beside the Adjusted EBITDA in the financial base. Credit implication: no evidence of extraction; control concentration cannot be assessed because holdings are undisclosed.

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for DXP ENTERPRISES INC (DXPE), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It combines the accepted source-readiness, financial-base and business-context work and covers financial risk, liquidity and business risk for the consolidated group, with current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025 in USD.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This synthesis relies mainly on the accepted upstream registers. A few inputs (acquisition cash flows, repurchases, cash a year earlier, the term loan rate) were read from the filings below, with locators given in the calculations. Locators are chunk pages (`page:N`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP's credit profile is moderately leveraged and improving, and the filings support an acceptable view with active monitoring. Its strongest support is liquidity of USD 411.0 million, a single term loan of USD 839.5 million that is not due until 2030, and gross leverage of 3.30x on last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, down from 3.76x at FY2025. The weakest point is that growth in pumping and water relies on cash-funded acquisitions that last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million does not cover, while cash taxes have been unusually low. What decides the outcome is whether organic growth holds, whether acquisitions and the new USD 150.0 million buyback authorisation are paid for without lifting net leverage, and how floating interest rates move, since the term loan is unhedged as of FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Assessment: DXP's fundamental credit view is acceptable and improving on gross leverage, flat on net leverage, with business risk below financial risk in importance. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium. Basis: the CP-1 leverage, liquidity, maturity and covenant tables and the CP-1A operating model, acquisition and governance rows. Medium rather than High because the covenant EBITDA bridge, the covenant level for two 2026 test dates, ownership and the credit agreement are missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis: A diversified, replacement-driven distributor with ample liquidity and no maturity before 2030 can carry its single floating-rate term loan, provided acquisition spending and distributions stay within cash generation. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, DXP's gross leverage fell from 3.76x at FY2025 to 3.30x at Q3 2026 on last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, but net leverage barely moved, from 2.41x to 2.44x, because total debt fell by only USD 7.3 million while cash fell from USD 303.8 million to USD 218.8 million after cash-funded acquisitions [CP-1 leverage table; calculations]. The improvement is therefore earnings-driven, and last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is not pro forma for acquired businesses, which is a modest conservatism in the ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, DXP has no maturity before October 13, 2030, when USD 812.0 million of term loan falls due, and the revolver, enlarged to USD 225.0 million and undrawn, runs to July 2, 2031 [CP-1 debt maturities and debt tables]. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is about 6.1 times the next twelve months of scheduled amortisation plus last-twelve-month cash interest, so near-term refinancing and debt service risk is low. Interest cover is 4.33x on cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, DXP's cash generation is flattered and does not fund its growth. Last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million benefits from cash taxes of USD 7.9 million against a provision of USD 35.4 million; with taxes at the provision, free cash flow would be USD 77.4 million. Acquisitions over the same twelve months absorbed USD 163.5 million, so the gap was met from cash, which the USD 205.0 million term loan add-on of December 2025 had raised (an analyst reading, since the filings give no use of proceeds) [CP-1 financials table and gaps; CP-1A transaction summary]. That pattern holds only while cash and availability remain ample.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, DXP's growth in Innovative Pumping Solutions is mostly purchased. In Q3 2026 that segment grew 43.3 percent in total but only 1.6 percent organically, and the same quarter's gross margin was lower than a year earlier, which management attributes in part to input costs [CP-1A operating model rows]. Service Centers, the largest segment, grew 11.3 percent organically.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, DXP's covenants leave wide room on reported numbers. Secured leverage is 2.30 to 1.00 against levels of 5.50 or 5.75 for the September 30, 2026 test, and the fixed charge ratio on the revolver is 2.98 to 1.00 against a minimum of 1.00 that only applies in a compliance period [CP-1 covenant table]. Covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million exceeds last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 254.4 million with no bridge in the filings, and the two filings disagree on the covenant level for two 2026 test dates [CP-0 conflicts]. Even a 30 percent fall in covenant EBITDA with net debt unchanged would leave secured leverage near 3.28x, well inside either level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, DXP has begun a new repurchase authorisation of USD 150.0 million after the prior programme lapsed with authorisation unused, while it keeps spending on acquisitions [CP-1A transaction summary]. The term loan limits distributions and investments through leverage-linked baskets whose levels are not printed, so the capacity to do both cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. DXP's revenue is spread across many accounts and product lines: over 90 percent of sales are products, no customer reached 10 percent of revenue, and the largest segment grew organically in Q3 2026 [CP-1A operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's liquidity is strong and its debt structure simple: USD 218.8 million of cash plus USD 192.2 million of revolver availability, one term loan of USD 839.5 million due in 2030, and no drawn revolver [CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's leverage and cover are moving the right way on a last-twelve-month basis, with gross leverage at 3.30x and cash interest cover at 4.33x against 3.76x and 4.20x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP has wide covenant headroom on reported ratios, and its issuer credit rating was raised by S&P from B to B+ on July 20, 2026 according to the company [CP-1A profile; no rating report supplied]. Category: Documentary Fact (issuer statement).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. DXP's debt is a single floating-rate term loan with no hedge disclosed as of FY2025, so rate moves flow straight into interest cost; the 10-K itself sized a 100 basis point move at USD 8.5 million before tax [10-K page:64; CP-1 debt table]. Category: Documentary Fact. DXP's growth in Innovative Pumping Solutions depends on acquisitions that are paid in cash and carry USD 30.7 million of contingent consideration, while organic growth in that segment is small [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation of the dependence. DXP's free cash flow quality is weaker than the headline because 2026 cash taxes were far below the provision and working capital absorbed cash as sales and acquisitions grew [CP-1 gaps; calculations]. Category: Analyst Interpretation. DXP's capital allocation path is undocumented in the filings: legal room for distributions, the covenant EBITDA bridge and ownership percentages are missing [CP-0 and CP-1A gaps]. Category: Insufficient Information. DXP's end-market exposure includes energy, which the 10-K lists as a covenant risk, and the latest backlog figure is from December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.
